topic: Sanad offices that give every client a portal to track their own cases are winning the retention game
format: Write a numbered list of 5 signs that a Sanad office has outgrown its current setup — make each one precise enough that most readers recognise at least four
post:
5 signs your Sanad office has outgrown its current setup:

1. You have a separate WhatsApp group for every client — and they're all pinging you at the same time.
2. A client asks "what's the status of our driver's work permit?" and you have to open three Excel tabs before you can answer.
3. You've missed a visa expiry not because you forgot — but because the renewal date was buried in a chat from six weeks ago.
4. You're invoicing from memory at the end of the month, guessing which services you actually completed for which company.
5. A client moved to another Sanad office. The reason they gave: "We just never knew what was happening."

That last one stings. Because the work was probably done. The permits were filed. The MOL submissions went through. But the client couldn't see any of it.

Sanad offices that give clients a portal — where they can log in and track every work permit, visa renewal, and Ministry of Labour filing themselves — aren't just winning on service. They're winning on retention.

Fewer 10 PM calls. Fewer angry WhatsApps. Fewer clients who leave not because you failed, but because they felt invisible.

The offices that figured this out aren't bigger. They just stopped making clients ask.
